_comment: Where the enumeration of Mistria's water bodies is read from.
This exists because the biggest gap in the dataset was self-inflicted. 113
fishing and diving windows said `habitats: ['pond']` and `locations: []`,
because 'Pond' is a class of place and expanding it into three concrete ponds
looked like an assertion the wiki had never made.
The wiki does make it. The Fishing page's 'Fishing Locations' section
enumerates every pond, river and ocean-reachable region, in a structured
list with `<div id="Pond">` anchors on it. So the set of ponds is a fact and
gets parsed like every other fact — what remains an inference is only whether
a *given* fish is in all of them, and that is what `confidence: "inferred"`
DIVABILITY IS AN EXCEPTION LIST. Two of the three ocean-reachable regions are
marked '(not divable)'. The page uses that parenthetical as its exception
marker, so an entry without one is divable. This matters: without it, a
diving window for an ocean fish would drop pins at The Western Ruins and
Sweetwater Farm, where the player cannot dive at all.
MINE FISHING FLOORS are narrower than the biome. The Upper Mines run 1-19 but
are only fishable from floor 2, and the Ancient Ruins' 81-99 excludes floor
90. Two ranges is two windows, which is what the OR-of-ANDs model is for.
_habitat_comment: HTML anchor id on the page -> the habitat it enumerates. The ids are there
so other pages can link to `Fishing#Pond`, which makes them a deliberate,
stable target rather than incidental markup.
